This appeal has been preferred against the Judgment of Conviction dated 17.01.2023 and Order of Sentence dated 24.01.2023 passed by the Court of learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act)-cum-Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Munger, in connection with POCSO Case No. 25 of 2018 (GR Case No. 287/2018) arising out of Muffasil P.S. Case No. 45 of 2018, whereby and whereunder the appellants have been convicted for the offence(s) punishable under Section(s) 366A and 342 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced for the said offence(s).
Patna High Court CR.

. Learned counsel for the appellants presses the prayer for bail made by the appellants under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.
4.

The main submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellants are that the appellants were charged for the offences punishable under Sections 366A, 342, 323, 376 read with Section 34 Pintu Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61118460/
1 of IPC and Section 8 of POCSO Act but convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 366A and 342 read with Section 34 of IPC and they were acquitted from the other charges.

entities.text: Pintu Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant namely Umesh Yadav has spent one year and seven months and other appellants have spent more than one year in jail and the major punishment awarded upon the appellants is five year of rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under Section 366A of IPC and so far as the merit of the allegation is concerned, the family members of the victim and appellants are agnates and relatives and admittedly, as per the evidence of P.W. 3, there was tensed relation in between both the parties at the time of alleged occurrence and in this regard, statements of P.W. 4 and P.W. 3 given by them in the cross-examination may be perused and furthermore, the victim made contradictory facts and allegations in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and the evidence deposed by her during trial and the main allegation of enticing the victim Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.1612 of 2023(3) dt.16-01-2024 away is against co-accused Sintu Yadav, in fact the said co- accused is still traceless and a counter case has been lodged in respect of his missing against the prosecution party and there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal of the appellants.
5.
Learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellants.

6. Considering the above submissions and mainly unlikelihood of the appellants' appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future, this Court is inclined to accept their prayer for bail made under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, let the appellants named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act)-cum-Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Munger, Bihar, in connection with POCSO Case No. 25 of 2018 (GR Case No. 287/2018) arising out of Muffasil P.S. Case No. 45 of 2018.

entities.text: Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act)-cum-Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Munger, Bihar
